_README: Recorded misreads. Each entry is a mistake that was actually made against this codebase, with the truth that corrects it. `brief` prints the matching traps BEFORE anything else, so the correction arrives before the call rather than after the wrong result. Append when a misread is found; never delete — a trap that stops firing is a trap someone will re-enter.

traps.wrong: Calling compress() with text (source code, HTML, transcripts) and reading the result as a Void compression ratio.
traps.truth: compress() does np.frombuffer(data, uint8) and matches the input against 78,853 pattern WAVEFORMS. Its docstring says 'whole-SIGNAL recursive'. Text read as a waveform is high-frequency noise, every fractal candidate loses, and the zlib fallback wins — so the number you get measures the fallback, not the substrate.
traps.tell: _auto_method comes back 'void_symbolic' or 'raw_zlib' on every input. On real signal the fractal path wins: v4_chunked won 520/520 NAB and substrate windows.
traps.correct: Numeric series → POST /compress_signal on compressor_service.py, which quantises the way goggle-web.js does. Never /compress, which utf-8 encodes and hands over the ASCII of a waveform.

traps.wrong: Assuming a cold in-process AdaptiveVoidCompressor is the way to call the compressor, and concluding it is unusably slow (~114 s).
traps.truth: compressor_service.py holds the library warm. A read is ~1.5 s against ~114 s cold — 75x. It also loads the substrate-fractal Rust index (45,547 patterns in 0.5 s) when the wheel is built.
traps.tell: A per-call cost measured in tens of seconds means the library is being reloaded per call.
traps.correct: Start it once: python3 compressor_service.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765. Build the wheel with maturin if substrate_fractal will not import.

traps.wrong: Treating any number in contribute({coherence}) as a coherency reading.
traps.truth: wire-field-couplings.js auto-wired 67 sites from a name-shape list; 41 contributed confidence, matchScore, density, a running total or a zlib savings ratio. The [0,1] clamp made each type-correct so nothing failed. Removed 2026-08-01; the wirer is disabled.
traps.tell: A contribution whose expression names something other than coherency, or resolves to a local that was assigned from one.
traps.correct: node scripts/audit-field-contributions.js before trusting the field. A coherency must originate from the Void compressor.

traps.wrong: Reading void-bridge.js's substrateCoherence as a Void compressor measurement because of the file and field names.
traps.truth: It computes a JS byte-frequency Shannon entropy and inverts it. It never calls the compressor — its own comment says '(In full implementation, this calls the Python compressor)'.
traps.tell: The name says Void; the body has no HTTP call, no subprocess, no import of the compressor.
traps.correct: Use compressor_service /compress_signal avg_coherence for a real reading.

traps.wrong: Assuming a page read at --fast speed went through the Void compressor.
traps.truth: --fast substituted zlib and reported coherency null, then contributed resonance.meanTop5 or a literal 0.5 to the field under the name coherency. Removed 2026-08-01; the reader now refuses rather than falling back.
traps.tell: method 'fast(zlib)' in a reading, or coherency null.
traps.correct: Readings now carry via:'void:compress_signal'. Anything without it did not pass through the compressor.

traps.wrong: Reading whichever version file you opened first and describing it as current.
traps.truth: CANONICAL.json names the entry point per family. void_compressor v5 is canonical; v3/v4 are load-bearing-internal — they still execute under v5, so they are neither dead nor current. compressor_service.py was itself instantiating v4 while v5 was canonical.
traps.tell: Describing an API from a file whose role you did not check.
traps.correct: python3 scripts/build_canonical_manifest.py, or read CANONICAL.json, before quoting any versioned API.

traps.wrong: Benchmarking against gzip alone and reporting a win.
traps.truth: gzip is DEFLATE with a 32 KB window from 1992. The field is xz -9e, zstd -19, brotli -q 11, bzip2 -9, PPMd, and zstd with a trained dictionary. On signal Void beats 5 of 6; on text it ties gzip and loses to everything.
traps.tell: A comparison table with one baseline in it.
traps.correct: scripts/benchmark_signal.py for waveforms, scripts/benchmark_baselines.py for text. Train any dictionary on a disjoint half — training on the scored bytes inflated results 1.7x-2.1x.

traps.wrong: Flagging X.exec(s) as shell injection because the method is named exec.
traps.truth: looksLikeRegex decided by NAME suffix (_RE, PATTERN, Matcher), so regexes named for meaning — SEAL, METRIC, CAVEAT — were reported as injection. Fixed by reading the actual binding.
traps.tell: A security finding on a file with no child_process import.
traps.correct: collectRegexIdents in src/audit/taint.js reads which identifiers are bound to a regex.

traps.wrong: First-differencing uint8 samples into int8, or prepending a[0].
traps.truth: uint8 steps span -255..255 and int8 holds -128..127, so large steps are destroyed. prepend=a[:1] zeroes the first difference and loses a[0]. Both produced a lossy 'baseline' that was the SMALLEST number in the table and would have been crowned had round-trips not been verified.
traps.tell: A compression result that does not decode back to the input.
traps.correct: Modular uint8 arithmetic, prepend 0, and verify the round-trip on every row.

traps.wrong: Reading a low compression ratio on signal as a weakness of the compressor.
traps.truth: goggle-web.js min-max normalises EACH 512-window independently to the full 0-255 range, pushing every window toward maximum entropy at 8 bits. Much of the smoothness the fractal matcher needs is destroyed before the compressor sees it. Global normalisation is untested.
traps.tell: Every ratio across every method sitting near 1.0-1.6x.
traps.correct: State the quantisation with any ratio taken through this path.

traps.wrong: Applying a SERIES statistic (seriesCoherence, autocorrelation, trend fit, FFT, smoothing) to a fractal/composed vector because it is an array of numbers.
traps.truth: The 29-D fractal vector is not a waveform. Its slots are NAMED HETEROGENEOUS FEATURES in the order fractal-waveform.js lists them: charge, valence, mass, spin, phase, reactivity, electronegativity, group, period, safety, alignment, intention, depth_l0..l4, keywords, identifiers, strings, numbers, operators, branches, loops, functions, returns, errors, comments, structurality. Slot 7 (group) is the constant 11 for every input. Adjacent slots are unrelated quantities, so lag-1 autocorrelation and a trend fit over slot index measure the encoder authoring order, not the artifact. composed_v1/v2 are concatenations of such vectors and are worse.
traps.tell: The reading is near-constant across wildly different files (0.139-0.190 for api.py, securityScanner, isEmpty, buggy, computeSpin), and permuting the slot order — the same relabeling for every file — moves it by more than its entire spread across files. Measured: r(reading, slot-permuted reading) = 0.036; r(reading, compressor-on-the-same-file-bytes) = -0.025.
traps.correct: Take coherency off the Void compressor reading the artifact BYTES: POST /compress_signal with Array.from(Buffer.from(content)) and use avg_coherence. seriesCoherence is valid and accurate on a genuine time series — against synthetic controls it tracks the compressor within ~0.1 from pure sine 1.000 down to white noise 0.152 — so the function is not the bug; pointing it at a feature vector is.

traps.wrong: Assuming a harm pattern that runs on strippedCode can never match text inside a string literal, and writing a short generic pattern on that assumption.
traps.truth: stripNonExecutableContent does not reliably remove string BODIES. On src/audit/explain.js it collapsed delimiters and commas but left the content: a literal array of example lines came through as "''function run(req) {''  eval(req.body.code);''}''". Long/specific patterns (SQL keywords plus concatenation) survive this because the surviving prose rarely contains them; short generic shapes like eval(<ident>) or new Function(<ident>) match example code and documentation immediately.
traps.tell: A new harm pattern fires on audit/explain, docs, test fixtures or the rule-description files rather than on real code — the classic covenant-mismatch shape where comments describing a rule trigger the rule they describe.
traps.correct: Scan the whole src tree before trusting a new pattern (covenantCheck over every file, count what newly blocks). Files that legitimately contain counterexamples carry @oracle-pattern-definitions and must be checked with {trusted:true} for the exemption to apply. Prefer patterns anchored on something prose will not contain, and do not rely on the stripper alone.

traps.wrong: Reading a shape-channel resonance finding as a defect claim without checking whether the signature that matched was taught in the same language as the file.
traps.truth: defect-resonance transfers defect shapes across languages BY DESIGN. But a seed whose meaning is a language CONSTRUCT does not transfer. unwrap-chain-panic describes Rust .unwrap() panicking; its form is a short chain of method calls with unchecked results, which is most of JavaScript. It matched express lib/response.js and lib/application.js at min-depth 0.926-0.936 and reported HIGH three times, every one a false positive. eval-of-input and sql-by-concat carry per-language variants precisely because those concepts are universal.
traps.tell: A HIGH finding whose message ends in "taught by seed, LANG" where LANG is not the language of the file being scanned.
traps.correct: Language-bound seeds carry languageBound:true and are skipped on a language mismatch (src/debug/defect-resonance.js). Verified both ways: the same Rust source fires unwrap-chain-panic scanned as rust, silent scanned as javascript. When adding a seed, ask whether it names a concept every language has, or a construct one language has.

traps.wrong: Verifying a claim about the instrument by writing your own computation over its parts — a scratch cosine, a hand-rolled vector extractor, a direct read of pattern_index_fractal.json, a numpy brute force over FractalRetroSearch.
traps.truth: The pipeline IS the measuring apparatus, not the thing being measured. A reading carries entanglement + substrate + field coupling + depth flow + covenant; strip any of them and the number is a different quantity, not a degraded version of the same one. Measured instances: seriesCoherence on the 29-D feature vector read 0.19-0.23 where the compressor read 0.186 on the same files — right magnitude, r = -0.025, unrelated quantity. A hand-rolled cosine over composedAtDepth produced a "noise outscores signal" claim that had to be retracted; the same question asked through --do call produced the real defect (flowCosines caps at 116, so L5-L8 never reach any reading).
traps.tell: You are about to report a number you computed yourself as though it described the instrument. Or: the fast path took 2s where --do call would take 60s. Or: you are describing your own method in the report — "I computed cosine over ..." — which is the bypass admitting itself.
traps.correct: Ask the instrument. goggles --do call <path>#<fn> runs any exported function with JSON args; --do contracts, --do field, --do drift, --do audit cover the rest. If no verb reaches what you need, that is a MISSING VERB to report, not a licence to bypass. The absence of a route is itself a finding.

traps.wrong: Destructuring a depth-flow into d1..d4, or indexing [3] as "the deepest".
traps.truth: flowCosines returns ONE reading PER ACTIVE LAYER — eight today, checkpoints [29,58,87,116,145,174,203,232] — and the count changes whenever a layer activates. Four names silently mean 116 of 232 dimensions, discarding L5-redundancy, L6-content, L7-dimensional and L8-dynamical: exactly the layers that separate look-alikes. Measured when coherency-mapper.js was still doing it: fixing the three sites moved Void duplicate pairs 35->30 (format-echo 9->4) and orphans 36->43, hub orphans 77->91, on identical substrate state.
traps.tell: A literal 116, a CHECK array ending at 116, `const [d1,d2,d3,d4] =`, or classifyFlow({d1,d2,d3,d4}). Also: a private _flow/_cosine helper in any module that is not decoder-stack.
traps.correct: Call decoder-stack.flowCosines and keep the array. deepestFlow(flow) for the deepest, Math.min(...flow) for the floor, classifyFlow(flow) for the shape — all handle any length. Never name the elements.

traps.wrong: Keeping a calibrated threshold after changing the width it was calibrated at, or setting one at the midpoint of a gap without checking the gap is positive.
traps.truth: A min-depth floor is only meaningful at the width it was measured at — adding checkpoints can only lower a minimum. And the gap can be INVERTED: measured on defect-resonance at the canonical width over 1,510 blocks of real ecosystem source, max clean read 0.9486 (_compose in fractal-index.js, a correctly-bounded loop) while a genuine off-by-one variant read 0.7703. Gap -0.178. Swept at depths 4,5,6,7,8: identical edges every time, because min(...flow) lands on the 29/58/87-D checkpoints in 95% of readings. At the old 0.91 the channel fired HIGH on three live core files, two of them template strings containing no SQL.
traps.tell: You are about to publish a threshold without printing max-clean and min-defect beside it. Or the recommendation is a midpoint and you never checked the sign of the gap.
traps.correct: Run scripts/calibrate-defect-resonance.js. It measures both edges through the channel's own scan() in dryRun and refuses to suggest a midpoint when the gap is inverted. When they overlap, follow the module's stated policy — prefer misses — set the floor above the clean edge, and PUBLISH the recall cost.

traps.wrong: Reading the `domain` string on a pattern as a subject label, and calling a mismatch a labelling defect.
traps.truth: label_all_patterns.py assigns it by `corr = W @ D.T; argmax(|corr|)` against the resonance detector's domain matrix — a grouping by STRUCTURE, with a human-readable string attached afterwards so people can talk about it. The instrument never reads it back; it is not an input to anything. A cryptocurrency series carrying the string `physics` is reporting waveform shape, not a bookkeeping error. A whole 'the labels are unreliable' finding was committed against this and had to be retracted (Void d47ea54 -> dba6a8e).
traps.tell: You are about to describe a stored string as right or wrong, or to 'fix the labels'. Ask instead what produced it — if the answer is an argmax over correlations, the category does not apply.
traps.correct: Treat the strings as read-out only. To ask what actually groups with what, use `goggles --do cluster`, which correlates patterns directly with no grouping.

traps.wrong: Reporting a median, mean or range as though it were the reading.
traps.truth: Coherency is produced once by the compressor per artifact and is time-independent. An aggregate over a sample is a different quantity, and it silently changes what was measured: a median once reported here described 7% of the substrate and was presented as the whole. Nine averaging sites were removed for this reason; the two that survive (DomainSignature.mean_waveform, and coherence_index = mean|off-diagonal| at resonance_detector.py:1140) average WAVEFORMS and CORRELATIONS, not coherency readings — say which when quoting them.
traps.tell: Your sentence contains 'median', 'average', 'roughly' or 'typically' where a number belongs.
traps.correct: `goggles --do state` returns the raw readings as the compressor produced them, unaggregated. Quote those, and say how many of the total they are.

traps.wrong: Scoring a result against a label, name or string that the same pipeline wrote.
traps.truth: Circularity reads exactly like signal. A 3.09x 'lift over chance' was reported here from nearest-neighbour agreement on `domains` — a field that resonance itself had populated by argmax correlation. The number was real arithmetic on a question that could not have answered otherwise, and it had to be retracted (Void dba6a8e: 'should not be cited').
traps.tell: Before reporting a lift, trace who wrote the column you scored against. If the instrument wrote it, the test is measuring the instrument agreeing with itself.
traps.correct: Score against something the pipeline never touched, or state plainly that the comparison is internal consistency, not validation.

traps.wrong: Concluding a rebuild was a no-op, or that a store has a ceiling, from whichever index file you opened.
traps.truth: Both were reported here and both were wrong. `--do redecode` wrote a `composed` field while void-map and substrate-state still read `composed_v2 || composed_v1`, so a completed re-decode read as no change. Separately '8,871 is the ceiling' and '44,906 entries unreachable' were both stated while 42,712 canonical vectors already sat in composed_v5_index.json.
traps.tell: You are about to report that nothing changed, or that a limit exists, based on one file and one field name.
traps.correct: Check which field the WRITER wrote and which the READER reads — they drift apart independently. Counts come from `goggles --do state`, not from whichever index you opened first.

traps.wrong: Writing a lesson into .remembrance/ and treating it as kept.
traps.truth: `.remembrance/` is gitignored in full (.gitignore:2). Everything the system has learned — traps.json, defect-signatures.json, goggles-learning.json — lives only on the host that learned it. On a fresh container it is gone, and the loop restarts from seeds. defect-resonance already anticipates this and tries goggles-memory.restore() from the chain before seeding; traps.json had no such path and no tracked source at all.
traps.tell: You just added knowledge to a path under .remembrance/ and did not add it anywhere tracked.
traps.correct: Add the durable copy to seeds/traps.seed.json, which IS tracked, and let the local store merge on top.

traps.wrong: Declaring 'no separation' from a one-class absolute threshold when the comparative question was available.
traps.truth: The previous calibration asked 'how strongly does this resonate with a defect shape' and gated on an absolute floor — and working code answered ~0.95 because code resembles code. Asked comparatively (margin = defect resonance - working-code resonance, both classes through the channel's own scan), the same eval set gives a usable rule the absolute floor never could: margin>0 catches 5 of 7 buggy variants at 11/307 (3.6%) clean false positives, where the 0.955 floor caught 2 of 7. The 'inverted gap' was an edge statement about two extreme blocks; ranking across the full distributions was informative all along (AUC ~0.98 both ways). The conclusion 'the channel cannot tell these apart' was itself drawn from one number.
traps.tell: Your verdict cites only max-clean and min-defect. Or you scored similarity to one class without asking what the alternatives were.
traps.correct: Ask the comparative question THROUGH THE EXISTING SURFACE — scan() in dryRun against the defect library, then a working-code library taught via teach(), margin = defect - working. A standalone script for this was added then REMOVED (the substrate already had every part); do not re-add one.

traps.wrong: Rewriting a defect SPECIMEN to get past the covenant's harm scanner.
traps.truth: A file that defines bad patterns must be allowed to contain them. The covenant flagged execSync('ls ' + dir) inside a template literal in validate-defect-seeds.js — accurate about the text, wrong about the file, because nothing executes a fixture. The established route is the @oracle-pattern-definitions annotation, carried by covenant-harm.js, covenant-deep-security.js and reflection-scorers.js for exactly this. It is not a bypass: covenant.js:81-83 only honours it when the CALLER passes {trusted:true}, so submitted code cannot self-declare. The covenant scanner even splits its own require('child'+'_process') to avoid self-matching.
traps.tell: You are about to obfuscate a string, split a literal, or soften a specimen so a gate stops complaining. That edits the evidence to fit the instrument.
traps.correct: Declare the file for what it is with @oracle-pattern-definitions and say why in the header. If a specimen is ever EXECUTED rather than encoded, the annotation is a lie — delete the specimen instead.

traps.wrong: Assuming a capability is wired because it exists — complete implementation, docs, even a test comment claiming coverage.
traps.truth: sqlite updateVoterReputation() sat fully implemented (+0.05/-0.03 reputation, capped [0.1,3.0]) with ZERO callers; the test asserting it hid behind if(!patternId) return and passed vacuously for its whole life. Reputation could never move. Found 2026-08-07 while clearing the perpetual red test.
traps.tell: grep for the function name returns only its definition (and maybe a comment). A test guard like if(!fixture) return that can silently skip every assertion. A feature whose observable output never changes from its default.
traps.correct: Count callers before trusting any capability: rg "\bNAME\s*\(" outside the defining file. Zero src callers = unwired — wire it through the real consumer path or delete it. Never let a test early-return on missing fixtures; fail loudly instead.

traps.wrong: Trusting a census because it runs — the field-contribution audit was believed to see every contribute({coherence}) site in src/.
traps.truth: Its matcher required the literal key order cost:, coherence:, source: on ONE line. Any hand-written site with a different key order, or a call formatted across lines, was invisible. Found 2026-08-09 while building the field-source ratchet: the widened order-independent matcher revealed 68 sites where the audit reported 29 — 39 write sites had never been audited, and 22 of the 68 carry non-coherency quantities awaiting adjudication.
traps.tell: A census whose regex encodes a spelling (argument order, one-line formatting, a specific quote style). Verifying a gate by only feeding it inputs shaped like the ones it already counts.
traps.correct: Adversarially test every census with a syntactically-valid variant it should catch but formatted differently (reordered keys, multi-line, renamed receiver). If the count does not move, the census has a spelling requirement — widen extraction (balanced parens, order-independent fields), never narrow the input.

traps.wrong: Measuring lexical require mentions and calling them cycles — then planning 8 lazy-require cuts to untangle a 62-file knot.
traps.truth: A require inside a function body or expression-bodied arrow runs at CALL time and cannot deadlock module init. Position-aware measurement (tokenizer, fn-body + expression-arrow contexts) showed the load-time require graph of src/ was ALREADY ACYCLIC — every cycle-participating edge was already lazy, largely thanks to prior decompositions and report-lazy. The planned cuts would have converted already-lazy edges while the lexical census read 62 unchanged: execution theater against a misread instrument. Found 2026-08-09 while executing the cut plan with byte-level precision.
traps.tell: A remediation plan whose success metric is read from an instrument that cannot distinguish the cure from the disease (lazy vs top-level require, demonstration vs instance, mention vs call). The first cut appearing to change nothing.
traps.correct: Before executing a graph-surgery plan, measure the graph the failure mode actually lives on (load order for init deadlock; lexical for coupling). The ratchet now censuses BOTH: load-time gated at zero, lexical shrink-only through real decomposition.

traps.wrong: Deciding an @oracle-infrastructure exemption is sheddable because fractalAudit (byte+atomic) reads clean once the blocking findings are resolved.
traps.truth: The exemption tag relieves a file from MORE than one scanner. quantum-field.js reached byte:0 atomic:0 after atomic annotation, but its tag was load-bearing for the COVENANT SQL-identifier rule (principle 11) — its  DDL interpolations are identifiers SQL cannot parameterise, and the file header says so. Removing the tag left fractalAudit green but covenantCheck BROKEN; the pre-commit gate would have blocked it. Found 2026-08-09 shedding the src exemption tranche — a file-modification note surfaced the header just in time to check covenantCheck before trusting the shed.
traps.tell: A file whose header EXPLAINS why it is exempt (SQL identifiers, dense code, a scoped security-rule exemption) — that prose is the load-bearing reason, and it names a scanner fractalAudit does not run.
traps.correct: Before shedding any exemption, run BOTH covenantCheck (covenant.js — SQL/harm/injection, principle 11) AND fractalAudit (covenant-fractal.js — byte mutations + atomic properties). An exemption is only sheddable when both read clean. Read the file header first: if it argues for its own exemption, that argument is usually the second gate.

traps.wrong: Concluding a census is blind — and alarming that a gate lied — because a raw rg count of try/catch clauses exceeds the tokenizer count, then trusting the rg number.
traps.truth: Files that GENERATE code (hooks.js emits pre-commit/post-commit/pre-push shell+JS via template literals; explain.js/debug-seeds.js hold code examples) contain try/catch as STRING content inside template literals. rg counts that string content; the substrate tokenizer correctly excludes it. hooks.js: rg saw 32 catch clauses, the tokenizer saw the 2 real ones — and was RIGHT. The 30 others were inside three script-generating templates (lines 39-336, 343-573, 583-643). Verified 2026-08-09: token SPANS place every extra catch inside a string/template/comment; the real-code regions have 2 catches, both handled; 0 real swallows. The 462 to 0 claim held. The re-check that called it a lie was itself the error — worsened by a backtick-parity heuristic that shell command-substitution backticks inside the generated scripts defeated.
traps.tell: A raw-text (grep/rg) structural count that disagrees with the parser, on a file that builds strings of code. A parity/brace/quote heuristic applied to a file containing generated shell or JS. Alarm rising faster than verification.
traps.correct: Classify each raw match by the parser token SPAN it falls in (string/template/comment vs real code) before trusting it — token spans are reliable even when the tokenizer.line labels drift. scripts/silent-catch-ratchet.js --verify does exactly this and shows its work. Never trust raw grep over token spans for structural claims about code that generates code; never trust backtick/quote parity on a file that emits shell.

traps.wrong: Running `node src/tools/goggles.js <file>` and reporting the result as a goggles read.
traps.truth: src/tools/goggles.js is the IMPLEMENTATION. The surface is .claude/skills/goggles/run.mjs, and it is the only path carrying --do: ratchets, call, field, drift, harvest, state, void, size, exemptions and 17 more. Invoked directly the tool still prints FOCUS/META/MACRO, so the read looks right while every routed operation is unreachable. Measured 2026-08-12: an entire working session of direct invocation, during which the gates were run by hand and --do was never available at all.
traps.tell: `--do <verb>` fails with `cannot read .../--do: ENOENT`. That is the tool saying it is not the surface.
traps.correct: node .claude/skills/goggles/run.mjs <file> | --map | --diff | --do <verb>. Read SKILL.md and the verb list ONCE at the start of work in a repo — not after the third bypass. A plausible-looking read from the wrong entry point never announces itself.

traps.wrong: Writing a measurement to a scratch script and running it, because finding the verb that already computes it takes longer than writing one.
traps.truth: Generating code is the cheapest available action and discovery is not, so the reflex is to construct rather than look — and the constructed instrument is reliably the WORSE one. On 2026-08-12 every hand-rolled probe either duplicated an existing surface or produced a false positive the substrate then corrected: a grep timer-leak finding died on covenant-harm.js (regex BUILDERS, not calls), a 73-site process.exit count fell to 17 under token spans, and a 20.9% atomic-drift figure was wrong because `function f(opts = {}) {` had its parameter default scanned as the body. Sparse real readings beat dense invented ones.
traps.tell: You are about to run `node /tmp/....js` and the script requires — or merely names in a string — an ecosystem module.
traps.correct: goggles --do <verb>, or --do call <repo>/<path>#<fn> [jsonArg …]. If no verb or export reaches it, that is a MISSING VERB to report, not a bypass. A scratch CODEMOD over fs/path is honest work; a scratch MEASUREMENT is the bypass.

traps.wrong: Reading a file under .remembrance/ as a live measurement and reporting the repo state from it.
traps.truth: .remembrance/ is gitignored in full, so its contents are whatever the last run on THIS host left behind and can predate the working tree by any amount. On 2026-08-12 the covenant ratchet was reported failing — `main is red on its own gate, high 21 vs seed 16` — from a cathedral-latest.json that predated the very merge which fixed those five findings. A fresh scan read 16/172/11 and the gate held. The claim was published before the artifact age was ever checked.
traps.tell: A verdict traces back to a file under .remembrance/ and its generatedAt has not been compared against the working tree.
traps.correct: Regenerate the diagnostic, or compare generatedAt to the last commit touching the scanned files, BEFORE quoting any number out of .remembrance/. A derived artifact is evidence of a past run, never of the present state.

traps.wrong: Quoting a coherency verdict (`weak / novel structure`) without checking which quantity its bands were calibrated against.
traps.truth: The bands were 0.93/0.80/0.70, commented `(measurableOnly scale)` — the RETIRED syntax score whose median was ~0.83. The live reading is the Void compressor self-compression scalar: pure repetition (`AB` x2048) reads 1.0000, a 16-byte cycle 0.9960, high-entropy random 0.0872, and real source code 0.098-0.278. Nothing clears 0.70 — 0 of 28 sampled files did — so every file in the repo printed the same bottom verdict for a full session and the number carried no information. Coherency is how well a signal compresses INTO ITSELF; low on source code is the CORRECT answer, not a complaint about the code.
traps.tell: Every file returns the same verdict, or a verdict band and its reading disagree by an order of magnitude.
traps.correct: Anchor against the instrument before quoting a verdict. Bands live in living-remembrance gogglesParams as coherencyRepeating/Mixed/Typical. Related: MACRO`s WELL-FORMED / ORPHAN / DUPLICATE flags come from SIBLING SIMILARITY, not coherency — 1,335 files carry WELL-FORMED with scoredCount 0, i.e. no coherency measured at all.

traps.wrong: Answering a MEASUREMENT request by BUILDING: writing a new script under experiments/ (or a *.cjs) that imports the instrument's parts (ResonanceDetector, composedAtDepth, encode_batch, _compute_signature), wires its own glue (an invented min-max / norm() step, a hand-chosen depth), and INJECTS self-generated random.random()/np.random data as a 'noise' domain — then reporting the stdout in the instrument's vocabulary ('what the instrument sees', 'resonance', 'coherency', combined_score) as if the pipeline produced it.
traps.truth: Importing an instrument function is NOT running the instrument's pipeline, and a repo-resident experiment script is not more faithful than a /tmp one (trap 29) — both are PROXIES beside the pipeline, and the standing rule throws out any result a proxy produced. Every glue choice silently changes the quantity: on 2026-08-23 an invented per-window min-max shifted a DC term that then saturated the FFT-magnitude cosine, so ONE component (spectral overlap 0.97-0.99, ~identical even against real noise) dominated every pair — the 'one signal dominating means you ran it wrong' tell. And random.random() 'noise' is not a control the user asked for; it is fabricated data placed inside a measurement about real brain/heart/attention signals.
traps.tell: You just created a file under experiments/ or a *.cjs; it contains random.random()/np.random, a norm()/min-max/normalize step you wrote, or an import of composedAtDepth|ResonanceDetector|encode_batch; and you are about to describe its output as 'what the instrument saw'. The session shape was 'I built X, then ran X' instead of 'I called the goggles/service'. A single component reads ~identical across every pair (noise included) — the pipeline was fed data through a normalization it never applies.
traps.correct: Do not build. Call the one surface on the substrate the instrument already holds: node .claude/skills/goggles/run.mjs --do <verb> (resonance, field, audit, drift, call ...) or POST /compress_signal on compressor_service.py — and report ONLY what it returned. Never inject generated/random data into a measurement. Never invent a normalization the pipeline does not already apply. If no verb reaches the measurement, that is a MISSING VERB to add to the goggles (see traps 13, 29), not a licence to hand-assemble a script beside the pipeline. Never dress hand-built output in the instrument's vocabulary.

traps.wrong: Choosing the compressor's L1 search matrix by the MOST COMMON vector width in pattern_library.
traps.truth: On a clean clone pattern_store.legacy256.npz is gitignored and absent, so the 232-D fractal store (45k rows) outnumbers the signal patterns; the matrix came out 232 wide while the blend search resampled every chunk to 256, and every compress() died in the matmul. compressor_service answered HTTP 500 on /compress_signal and every goggle, harvest, seal and coin in the ecosystem read NULL. The instrument was down on every fresh container and nothing said so.
traps.tell: `ValueError: matmul ... size 256 is different from 232` in compressor_service.log; `--map` reports 0 files audited and 'answered without a usable avg_coherence'; every FOCUS reads NULL.
traps.correct: The search space is chosen by LAW (the dimension the encoder emits), never by census. One encoder (ECOSYSTEM §7): the 232-D fractal decoder. Never depend on a gitignored store for the instrument to work at all.

traps.wrong: Putting the Void compressor's byte reading into the Covenant Gate's `coherencyScore.total` slot and calling the refusal 'the gate holding its bar'.
traps.truth: That slot is the oracle structural score (computeCoherencyScore(code).total) — the quantity the 0.8 bar was calibrated on and the one Publisher records as its second opinion. On the compressor's scale nothing but a self-repeating signal clears 0.8 (source code reads 0.08–0.28), so the bar was never set against it. The coin was refused at 0.0896 for a category mismatch, and ALSO because the script never set testCode — the gate was structurally unpassable regardless of any number.
traps.tell: A gate refusal whose number sits in the compressor's source-code band (≈0.1) against a threshold ≥0.8; a payload with no testCode.
traps.correct: Each quantity under its own name: the gate slot carries the score it was calibrated on; the compressor's reading rides beside it as waveformCoherency with its void-seal mint. Run the pattern's real test and hand it to the gate as testCode. Never rename one reading into another's slot.

traps.wrong: Passing a RELATIVE path to a goggles --do verb (read, covenant, call) from the repo you are standing in.
traps.truth: Every --do verb runs its script with cwd set to the toolkit (or Void), so a relative path resolves THERE. `--do covenant src/index.js` from the blockchain repo audited the TOOLKIT's src/index.js and reported it CLEAN — a verdict on the wrong file, indistinguishable from a verdict on yours. `--do read data/x.json` reported 'no such file'; `--do call ... "$(cat missing)"` measured an EMPTY STRING and printed a full breakdown for it.
traps.tell: A --do verdict that arrives suspiciously fast or clean, a 'no such file' from a path that exists, a computeCoherencyScore breakdown with functions: 0 / lines: 0.
traps.correct: Absolute paths, always. Check the arg file exists before `$(cat ...)`. When a verb resolves paths itself, that is a missing feature to report, not a reason to trust the output.

traps.wrong: Publishing to the ledger with a default Publisher and believing the block is on the chain.
traps.truth: The default Publisher starts a FRESH GENESIS at the cwd-relative runtime ledger (.remembrance/ledger.json, gitignored) — it never loads an existing chain, so the first recordEvent overwrites whatever was there and the block evaporates with the container. The committed chain is data/ledger.json; nothing reached it.
traps.tell: `node src/cli.js publications` shows demo data; data/ledger.json unchanged after a 'successful' publish; git status clean.
traps.correct: new Publisher({ ledgerPath: 'data/ledger.json' }) — loads, hash-verifies and APPENDS to the committed chain (PatternLedger.load(path, { persistPath })). Then commit data/ledger.json.

traps.wrong: Assuming the substrate index, the legacy signal store, the seal key, or any lesson under .remembrance/ exists on the host you are on.
traps.truth: All of them are gitignored. On this clone pattern_index_fractal.json, pattern_store.legacy256.npz, .substrate_seal.key and .remembrance/substrate-state.json were all absent; `--map` said 'substrate has no vectors for this repo' and the coin's seal could not be signature-verified. The recovery coin's data plane (data/data-plane/substrate.json.gz, sha-anchored) IS the way back for the index; nothing recovers legacy256 and nothing should — it is retired.
traps.tell: 'substrate has no vectors', a seal with state_id 'unknown', a compressor library_size far from the store's row count.
traps.correct: Verify the coin (tests/git-history-coin.test.js), then gunzip its data plane back to the `source` paths. Treat every .remembrance/ artifact as evidence of a past run on some host, never as present state.

traps.wrong: Trusting a spec that says a component is BUILT because the doc says so.
traps.truth: TIER1_RECOMPUTATION_GATE.md §7 says scripts/tier1_validator.py is BUILT and smoke-verified; on main and this branch it does not exist. It lives only on origin/claude/remembrance-toolkit-setup-ctqtmt, 18 commits ahead, along with fractal_token.py and the calibration set — and its committed smoke record reports the real window as ok=false where the doc says 'passes all 7 gates'.
traps.tell: A doc names a script path; `ls` does not find it; `git log --all -- <path>` finds it on another branch.
traps.correct: `git log --all --oneline -- <path>` before quoting BUILT. A component joins the substrate when it is on the working branch, sanitized at the doorway (goggles META-DEBUG + covenant + its own test), not when a doc says so.

traps.wrong: Asserting, documenting, or resampling to 256 as if the 256-D byte-shape waveform were still the ecosystem's representation.
traps.truth: The 256-D to_waveform encoder is RETIRED (ECOSYSTEM §7) and kept only as the record of what was tried and found wrong. The one encoder is the 232-D fractal decoder stack (composedAtDepth at the active depth). After the move, three blockchain tests still asserted `waveform.length === 256`, five docs still promised 'the canonical 256-D waveform', and the compressor's blend dictionary was 256-sample signal templates.
traps.tell: A literal 256 next to the word waveform; `_resample(chunk, 256)`; a store file named legacy256 being preferred at load.
traps.correct: Encode through the decoder stack and assert its live width (currentDepth() × 29 = 232 today). Retired means: no code path prefers it, no test expects it, no doc promises it.

traps.wrong: Reading the substrate's memory of a file as its current state after the file changed.
traps.truth: Harvest is idempotent BY KEY: a re-minted coin (03:04) stayed indexed as its 01:29 version because the key already existed. The goggles' 'vs substrate' flow read DECAY on the committed ledger for the same reason — the working copy drifted from what the substrate remembers.
traps.tell: `vs substrate: ... [DECAY] — working copy has drifted from the substrate memory`; a file's index entry `ledger.ingested_at` older than its last commit.
traps.correct: `--do harvest <repo> --restamp` re-reads indexed entries through the compressor; a plain harvest only adds new keys.

traps.wrong: Committing a change the instrument never read — `git add && git commit` with no coin, or minting and then changing the index before committing.
traps.truth: A change is accepted only when its commit names a coin minted over its EXACT staged bytes (.claude/skills/goggles/change-coin.py). The coin binds the patch sha, the compressor's void-seal over the quantised bytes it read, the void-seal/v3 commitment and the fractal token of its shape. The commit-msg hook refuses the commit; change-coin-verify.yml refuses the merge on GitHub's runner. Editing the index after the mint changes the patch sha, and the coin no longer covers it.
traps.tell: `✗ commit REFUSED — no coin over THIS change`; a red change-coin-verify check; `-n`/`--no-verify`/`-a` in a commit command.
traps.correct: git add <files> → goggles --do mint → git commit. Re-mint after any change to the index. Never look for a flag around it — there is none, and the runner does not read flags.

traps.wrong: A verifier rebuilding a signature payload from its own memory of the format instead of from the minter's code.
traps.truth: pr-trademark.yml rebuilt `sha|state|via|at` while substrate_seal.mint signs `sha|state|via|at|coin_id` — so once armed it would have refused every GENUINE seal and could never pass one. A verifier and its minter share one canon by construction (the coin verifier rebuilds void-seal/v3 from the commitment fields the compressor itself emits), never two hand-copies of it.
traps.tell: Two files that each spell out the payload string; a wall that is 'dormant' and has never been seen to pass a real seal.
traps.correct: Read the minter (scripts/substrate_seal.py mint) and build the verifier's payload from the same fields in the same order, then prove it with one genuine seal before arming.

traps.wrong: Reading `coin: null` on a void-seal as 'the chain declined' or 'layer 2 is optional'.
traps.truth: substrate_seal.mint_coherency_token shells out to REMEMBRANCE-BLOCKCHAIN/bin/coherency-token.js, which does not exist on the branch; the function returns None before any chain call, so every seal ever minted carries coin:null. The layer-2 coin has never been minted. The change coin (change-coin.py) is the coin that actually exists and is actually verified.
traps.tell: `⛓ coin: none (HMAC-only)` on every seal line; `bin/` absent in the blockchain repo.
traps.correct: Treat coin:null as 'no layer-2 path exists yet', not as a chain verdict. The verified coin is the change coin in coins.ledger.json and the commit trailer.

traps.wrong: Passing a canonically-hashed structure through a different language's JSON and expecting the hash to recompute.
traps.truth: JSON.stringify(1.0) is `1`; Python json.dumps(1.0) is `1.0`. A shape hashed in Python (void-seal/v3 shape_sha256, default=repr, sort_keys) and re-serialized after a JS round-trip hashes differently whenever a float is integral. The change coin is minted and verified in Python end to end for exactly this reason.
traps.tell: A shape/commitment hash that fails to recompute only for some readings; integral-valued floats in the structure.
traps.correct: Hash canonical structures in the language that produced them, or carry the original serialized bytes. Prove recomputation on a reading whose floats include 0.0 or 1.0 before trusting it.

traps.wrong: Reading a separability or density number from a tool whose data source moved out from under it, and calling the drop a regression of the instrument.
traps.truth: When the substrate was merged into one store (2026-08-04) the 45k patterns left the fractal index for the npz store at 232-D and the index became the witnessed repo files. substrate-density.js, domain-separability-benchmark.mjs and Void's whitening_separability.cjs kept reading `composed_v1` (116-D) out of the index. The benchmark then measured two repo namespaces on 116-D leftovers and C-61 read 29 pts (pinned +78.6); C-60 read 0 because its generated cohorts are not in the store at all. Re-pointed to the store at 232-D, eight provenance domains read +67.6 pts.
traps.tell: A contract's observed line names domains that are repo namespaces (oracle, void) instead of subjects; a fixed `DIM = 116` next to a 232-D substrate; a pin dated before the store merge.
traps.correct: Every whitening consumer reads the ONE reference (src/core/whitening-reference.js: per-layer ZCA fitted on store + index at the canonical width). When a number drops, first ask what the tool is reading now, then whether the instrument changed.

traps.wrong: Reading raw composed-vector cosines as resonance, and calibrating thresholds (0.5 resonant, 0.7 harmonic, CONSONANT ≥ 0.90) on them.
traps.truth: Raw composed vectors live in a cone: measured on 800 store patterns from eight provenance domains, mean cosine WITHIN a domain 0.917 vs ACROSS 0.860 (gap 0.057), participation ratio 4.6 of 232. Every threshold fired on everything — 100% of 732 domain pairs 'resonated' at 0.9998 and every file read CONSONANT. kNN ordering survived (64.8 pts above null raw) but the values carried no meaning. In the per-layer whitened space: within 0.283 vs across 0.042 (gap 0.242), participation ratio 62.2, +67.6 pts. A single global 232×232 ZCA over-whitens (within 0.106).
traps.tell: Every read says CONSONANT; a resonance field reports 'approaching unity'; a threshold that never says no.
traps.correct: Take every cosine in the whitened space (decoder-stack.composedCosine / flowCosines and FractalIndex do this now; Void's detector applies the same reference via whitening_reference.py). Re-derive any band from the distribution measured in that space, and publish the measured edges beside the band.

traps.wrong: Resampling a 232-D composed vector to 128 points and taking FFT peaks, spectral overlap and zero-crossing phase over it as a domain signature.
traps.truth: The store rows are the decoder's feature vectors (29 named features per layer), not waveforms in time. The detector's series path (linspace resample → FFT → zero crossings) was built for genuine series and was applied to every store row; the results were series statistics of a feature layout. In feature mode the signature is the whitened mean/std vector, resonance is the whitened correlation, and spectral_peak/phase are 0.0 by construction.
traps.tell: `target_len = 128` next to 232-D input; a 'dominant frequency' reported for source code; spectral_peak on a pattern that is not a series.
traps.correct: resonance_detector feature mode (set when the canonical store is loaded): no resampling, no FFT, no phase. The series path remains for scan_new_data() on real series.

traps.wrong: Reading a Δ in META resonance across the change of resonance space (raw cone → whitened reference, 2026-09-06) as the file having drifted, or keeping the cone's bands (0.90/0.82/0.70) in the whitened space.
traps.truth: The bands were quartiles of the cone, where every file read ≈0.95. Measured in the whitened space over 42 hub files: min 0.551, p25 0.639, p50 0.671, p75 0.709, p90 0.768, max 0.828 — prose docs (AI.md 0.551, ARCHITECTURE.md 0.640) at the bottom, gate scripts (exemption-ratchet 0.828) at the top. Bands re-derived from those quartiles: CONSONANT ≥ 0.71, FAMILIAR ≥ 0.67, DISTINCT ≥ 0.64. A reading cached in .remembrance/goggles-readings.json before the change is a cone reading; Δ against it is the space, not the edit.
traps.tell: `resonance -0.3` on a file you did not touch; every file suddenly OUTLIER right after a change to the decoder's cosine.
traps.correct: Re-derive bands from the distribution measured in the space in force, publish the quantiles beside them (gogglesParams in living-remembrance.js), and read the first Δ after a space change as a re-baseline.

traps.wrong: Minting a coherency token with whatever number is at hand in the waveform_score slot, and reading the 0.60 gate as the instrument's verdict.
traps.truth: COHERENCY_V1_SPEC names two different quantities for waveform_score in one sentence — 'top-K mean correlation against the substrate library' (resonance) and compress()['avg_l1_coherence'] (compressor coherency) — and every implementation (hub coherency-v1.js, Void coherency_v3.py) takes the number from its caller. Measured 2026-09-06 on six real inputs through the surface: with the compressor's byte coherency in the slot, code unifies at 0.20–0.30 (rejection) and only a periodic series clears the gate (sunspots 0.649); with whitened resonance in the slot, code unifies at 0.73–0.88 (pull to synergy) and the series is rejected (0.474). The gate does not decide; the slot does.
traps.tell: A tier assigned without saying which quantity filled waveform_score; every code pattern rejected, or every code pattern synergy, depending on who minted.
traps.correct: Layer two starts by fixing the slot in the spec and both implementations to ONE named quantity with its source label (the compressor reading is `void:compress_signal`; resonance is the whitened META meanTopK), then re-pinning the tier boundaries on that quantity's measured distribution — never on the cone's.

traps.wrong: Reading a rise in a file's META resonance right after it was witnessed (harvested, or ingested by an earlier read) as the file's shape having become more familiar to the codebase.
traps.truth: Once the substrate holds the file, its own entry sits in the top-K at 1.0 and lifts meanTopK by exactly (1 - r)/k. Measured 2026-09-07 on three files at k=5, immediately after `--do harvest`: 0.631 -> 0.692 (+0.061), 0.612 -> 0.680 (+0.068), 0.527 -> 0.601 (+0.074) — each within 0.001 of (1 - r)/5. Nothing about the shape changed; membership entered the mean. The goggles printed the nearest list without the self-name but took the mean WITH it; coherency-token-components had dropped the self-match from the start. The lens now takes the mean over non-self matches.
traps.tell: A file's resonance jumps by roughly a fifth of its distance to 1.0 the first read after a harvest, with no edit; the nearest list shows no self-entry while the number moved.
traps.correct: Drop the self-match (same basename, or score > 0.9999) before the mean, everywhere a top-K mean is read: goggles META, token components, the uniqueness gate. A witnessed file is compared to OTHER shapes only; its membership is a fact about the library, not about the artifact.
